title: Climbing Kilimanjaro Solo: How It Works
excerpt: You can climb Kilimanjaro as a solo traveller, either privately with your own crew or by joining others. Here is how it works.
body:
You cannot climb Kilimanjaro without a licensed guide, but you can certainly go as a solo traveller. There are two ways to do it.

## A private climb

You have your own guide, cook and porters. You set the pace, and the dates are completely yours. It is more expensive per person, because the crew is not shared.

## Joining a small group

On certain dates, climbers can join a group on a fixed departure. You share the crew and meet other people. The dates are fixed and the pace is the group's pace, although guides split up when needed.

## Is it safe as a solo traveller?

Yes. You are never alone on the mountain: your guide and crew are with you all the time. Many solo women climb Kilimanjaro. Tell us if you have specific wishes, for example about guides.

## What solo climbers enjoy

- Time to think and enjoy silence.
- Real contact with the crew: you learn more Swahili and more about life in Tanzania.
- Full flexibility in planning before and after.

## Tips

- Choose a single tent; usually included for solo climbers.
- Bring a book or downloaded podcasts for the afternoons.
- Combine with a [solo-friendly safari](/blog/solo-traveller-safari/).

[Plan your solo climb](/travel-proposal/) and tell us whether you prefer private or a group.
